title: Universe classifier axes record v0.3.0
description: ADR-130. Successor to universe_classifier_axes_record@0.2.0. Exactly one bound moves: supported_claim rises from 200 to 300 characters. evidence stays at 12 objects, quote stays at 1200 characters, and every axis, enum value, pattern and required field is byte-equivalent to 0.2.0. The V2.3 calibration stopped after three rows, and all three carried exactly one schema error apiece -- a supported_claim of 233, 204 and 204 characters against the 200-character cap -- while their quote lengths (972, 829, 994) and evidence counts (12, 12, 8) were all inside the 0.2.0 ceilings and every one of their 32 evidence objects carried a legal axis label. The 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 contracts stay byte-identical so each earlier run's evidence remains interpretable under the contract that run actually used. Note that 0.3.0 is a widening: every valid 0.2.0 axes object is a valid 0.3.0 one, so a version is separated from its neighbours by its route's filenames and const bindings, never by schema validity alone. ADR-126. Exactly what the model returns for one firm: economic axes and the evidence for them. There is deliberately no tier field of any name. A tier is derived afterwards by a versioned deterministic engine from these axes, so a prompt revision can never silently move tier membership, and a model that emits a tier is refused rather than obeyed. Every array and string is bounded, because the run is held to the committed max-output-token contract and compactness is a contract term, not a preference.

customer_market_orientation.description: Descriptive metadata only. The deterministic tier engine takes this as no input at all.
